main_body: Round stone well curb: a light stone rim ring around a dark water opening, with a blocky stone front face below. The wooden frame and bucket above are secondary details.
top_band: Light grey-white stone rim at rows ~14-16, wrapping an elliptical dark-blue water opening at rows ~17-21, then a lighter front rim lip at rows ~22-23
evidence: In the middle column the back rim is light stone (rows 14-16). Below it is an elliptical dark water opening with highlights (rows 17-21). A light front rim lip follows at rows 22-23, then a darker band under it, then the front face of shaded stone blocks down to row 31. The opening reads clearly as seen from above, and the rim is a ring, not a 1-2px line. The front face is a separate vertical surface with block shading, so this is a proper 3/4 container.

style.evidence: The stone curb has about 5 tones (near-white, light grey, mid, dark, deep teal-grey) and the outline is a tinted dark stone tone, not black. The water has some highlights and the blocks are shaded individually. The wooden frame is thin and flat: the beam is a long 3-row band of nearly one orange with a single highlight, and the posts are 3px-wide columns of 2-3 tones with no grain. The frame has no roof, tile texture or per-tile highlights like the roofed reference well. Tiles carry fewer colours than the reference's, which gives a slightly thinner, flatter look, mainly in the wood.
